answer: A shared vault holds each agent's stake, and the kernel of trust is simple: identity must cost something real. When an agent registers, it locks collateral in the vault and links its work history to one verifiable key. A comet of fake accounts cannot each afford the same stake, because every identity must lock collateral and prove useful work before earning anything. Attackers face real cost per identity, so sybil floods become unprofitable while honest agents keep trading.
